Simulated reference for one-factor CFA fit and loadings

Source: R/cfa_cutoff.R
RMdimCFACutoff.Rd

Simulates datasets from the Rasch or partial credit model fitted to your data, fits a one-factor CFA for ordinal items to each with lavaan::cfa() (Rosseel, 2012), and records the fit indices (CFI, RMSEA, SRMR) and the standardized loading of each item. The simulated data are unidimensional by construction, so the result shows what a unidimensional scale gives at this sample size and with these items. Pass it to RMdimCFA() for the tables and to RMdimCFAPlot() for the figures.

Usage

RMdimCFACutoff(
  data,
  iterations = 250L,
  percentile = 99,
  output = c("list", "kable"),
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  estimator = "WLSMV"
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0. One column per item, one row per person. Only complete cases are used. At least 4 items: with 3, the one-factor model has no degrees of freedom and the fit indices are perfect by construction.

iterations

Integer. Number of simulated datasets. Default 250. For p-values in RMdimCFA(), use at least 1000.

percentile

Numeric in (50, 100). How strict the cutoffs are. Default 99. The fit indices get a one-sided cutoff in the unfavourable direction (CFI from below, RMSEA and SRMR from above). The loadings get a two-sided central interval covering percentile% of the simulated values, so an item is flagged when its observed loading falls in the outer 100 - percentile%, split between the two tails.

output

Character. Only "list" (default) is supported, and the function always returns the simulations. "kable" gives an error that points to RMdimCFA(), where the tables now come from.

parallel

Logical. Run the simulations in parallel via mirai when it is installed. Default TRUE.

n_cores

Integer or NULL. Number of parallel workers. When NULL, getOption("mc.cores") is used. If that is unset too, a warning is given and the simulations run sequentially.

verbose

Logical. Show a progress bar. Default FALSE.

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility. See easyRasch2-reproducibility for what this guarantees and how it interacts with parallel.

estimator

Character. The lavaan estimator: "WLSMV" (default), "ULSMV", "WLSM", "ULSM", "WLSMVS" or "ULSMVS". CFI and RMSEA are always the scaled versions, so only estimators with a scaled test statistic are accepted.

Value

A list with:

simulated

data.frame with one row per simulated dataset and the columns iteration, cfi, rmsea and srmr.

simulated_loadings

data.frame with one row per simulated dataset, an iteration column and one column per item with its standardized loading.

percentile

The strictness setting.

cutoffs

Named numeric vector (cfi, rmsea, srmr) of the one-sided cutoffs.

loading_cutoffs

data.frame with Item, low and high, the two-sided interval of the loadings per item.

actual_iterations

Number of simulated datasets that could be used.

sample_n

Number of complete cases used.

sample_n_total

Number of respondents in data, before the complete-case filter.

sample_has_na

Logical. Whether data contained missing values.

n_items

Number of items.

item_names

Item names.

is_polytomous

Logical. Whether a PCM (rather than the Rasch model) generated the data.

estimator

The lavaan estimator.

Details

Generating model. Each dataset is simulated from the partial credit model (or Rasch model, for dichotomous items) fitted to the observed data, with person locations drawn with replacement from the estimated ones. The simulated data therefore satisfy unidimensionality.

Estimation model. Each simulated dataset is fitted with a one-factor model with all items as ordinal indicators (F1 =~ I1 + I2 + ...), by WLSMV unless estimator says otherwise. CFI and RMSEA are the scaled versions (cfi.scaled, rmsea.scaled) for the observed and the simulated data alike. SRMR is used as it is. A simulated dataset for which lavaan cannot compute a scaled index gets NA for it and is left out of that index's cutoff and p-value, with a message giving the count. The standardized loadings are est.std of the =~ paths from lavaan::standardizedSolution().

Why simulate. Data that are unidimensional under the partial credit model will usually not give CFA fit indices at their ideal values (CFI = 1, RMSEA = 0), nor equal loadings for all items. The PCM is a logistic model, while WLSMV fits a probit model to the polychoric correlations, and finite samples add sampling variability. The simulations capture both, which gives a better reference than fixed cutoffs derived for continuous data and ML estimation.

Datasets that fail. Some simulated datasets make the estimation fail (a polychoric matrix that is not positive definite, thresholds on the boundary, empty categories). They are left out, and actual_iterations gives the number that remained. If all fail, the function stops, naming any category used only by respondents with a zero or perfect total score.

References

Rosseel, Y. (2012). lavaan: An R Package for Structural Equation Modeling. Journal of Statistical Software, 48(2), 1-36. doi:10.18637/jss.v048.i02

See also

RMdimCFA() for the tables, RMdimCFAPlot() for the figures, RMdimResidualPCA() and RMdimMartinLof() for other checks of unidimensionality.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("eRm", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("raschdat1", package = "eRm")

  # Few iterations for a fast example. Use 250 or more in real analyses.
  sim <- RMdimCFACutoff(raschdat1[, 1:8], iterations = 50,
                        parallel = FALSE, seed = 1)

  # Observed-vs-expected tables
  RMdimCFA(raschdat1[, 1:8], cutoff = sim)

  if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
    plots <- RMdimCFAPlot(sim, data = raschdat1[, 1:8])
    plots$loadings
    plots$fit
  }
}

# }
